evidence_rule: Only the cited route, selection record, rights evidence and pinned Eurostat fact pack may support these briefs. Missing source-specific numeric fixtures remain explicit blockers.

briefs.question: What does the reserves-to-production ratio say about remaining fossil-fuel reserves?

supported_answer_boundary.statement: The series is a conditional reserves-to-production measure: it relates recorded reserves to production under the source's definitions and assumptions. It is not a countdown forecast, a prediction of depletion, or a statement that production will remain constant.
supported_answer_boundary.numeric_claims_blocker: A source-specific OWID data fixture, exact indicator definition, unit, geography scope and observation period are not present in the current repository evidence. V2-06 must lock them before any value or trend is written.

unit_period_scope.unit: years, subject to confirmation from the source indicator metadata
unit_period_scope.period: source-defined first and last observation; pending source-specific fixture
unit_period_scope.geography: source-defined entities; do not imply a global aggregate

transformation.description: Display the reviewed source series without recomputing a depletion date. Any chart rounding must be presentation-only.

limitations: Reserves are estimates defined by the source and can change with discoveries, prices, technology, reporting and revisions.
A reserves-to-production ratio is conditional on the measured reserves and production definitions; it does not say when the world will run out.
Countries and fuels may use different coverage, reporting quality and observation periods.
Raw-data redistribution remains unverified in the current pilot selection and must not be promised.
additional_cite_supply_value: Make the conditional meaning and limitation visible beside the source chart.
Keep the source, observation coverage and citation in one publisher-facing page.
Expose only the embed action supported by the reviewed rights record.

internal_link_targets.purpose: related energy-cost series; link only as a related comparison, not a causal claim

briefs.question: How have inflation-adjusted solar photovoltaic module prices changed over the available series?

supported_answer_boundary.statement: The page may explain what the source's photovoltaic-module price series measures and how its currency, price basis, unit and period should be read. It must not describe a trend until the source series and adjustment metadata are pinned.
supported_answer_boundary.numeric_claims_blocker: The repository contains the checked OWID chart URL and seed catalogue entry, but not a locked source-data fixture with currency basis, inflation treatment, unit and observation period.

unit_period_scope.unit: price per watt, subject to confirmation from source metadata
unit_period_scope.period: source-defined first and last observation; pending source-specific fixture
unit_period_scope.geography: series-defined global or entity scope; must be stated from the fixture

transformation.description: Preserve the source's currency and inflation basis. Cite Supply may round for display only and may not silently convert currencies or rebase prices.

limitations: Price series may combine or revise historical source methods; the source's metadata and version must be visible.
A module price is not the same as a complete installed-system cost, generation cost or household electricity price.
Currency, inflation adjustment and unit basis materially affect comparisons.
Raw-data redistribution is unverified because the source review records mixed underlying terms including IRENA copyright.
additional_cite_supply_value: Put the price basis, source date and limitations next to the chart rather than leaving them to an external page.
Give publishers a stable citation and reviewed embed route.
Prevent a module-price series from being mistaken for a full solar-system cost.

internal_link_targets.purpose: related energy indicator; no shared trend claim

briefs.question: What do the EU renewable-energy indicators measure across the covered energy-balance categories?

supported_answer_boundary.statement: The dataset contains separate annual percentage indicators for defined EU27 energy-balance categories. The indicators have different denominators and must be read as separate measures, not added into one total.
supported_answer_boundary.numeric_claims_scope: Only facts from the pinned nrg_ind_ren snapshot and approved metric IDs may be shown. The current fact pack covers EU27_2020 annual observations from 2020–2024 for the approved categories.
supported_answer_boundary.explicit_exclusion: Do not use the provisional 2025 observation in comparisons; transport is absent in that period in the pinned scope.

unit_period_scope.unit: percentage of the source-defined energy measure
unit_period_scope.period: annual, 2020–2024 in the pinned fact pack
unit_period_scope.methodology_note: 2020–2021 is a noted methodology break; trend claims should use 2021 onward or explain the discontinuity.

transformation.description: Resolve only approved metric IDs from the pinned JSON-stat response; preserve source dimensions and round only at display time.
transformation.numeric_calculation_allowed: only the approved transformation in the fact pack

limitations: The category percentages use different denominators and must not be summed.
Eurostat status flags, provisional observations and the methodology break must remain visible when relevant.
The asset page is a narrow dataset reference; it must not duplicate the broader interpretation in the existing EU-renewables insight.
The exact source data and reuse conditions remain subject to the cited Eurostat evidence and attribution requirement.
additional_cite_supply_value: Keep the EU27 scope, unit, period and category dimensions visible beside the data.
Make the methodology break and provisional-data boundary explicit.
Provide a marketplace-rendered embed that matches the reviewed Eurostat rights path.

internal_link_targets.purpose: broader interpretation; keep this asset page narrower and dataset-specific
